PRACTICE MATERIAL - ENGINE PROGRAM



Engine Pop Quizzes
11 quizzes - one per course - covering all 85 modules in the engine completion sheet.

Name:                                                       Date:



   How to use: Take one quiz after finishing a course. Circle the best answer (A-D), then check your answers in
   the separate Answer Key section at the back of this pack. Review the module named under any question you
   missed. Untimed on the first run; repeat the quiz later and aim for 9/10 or better.



COURSES IN THIS PACK

    1. Course 1 - Engine Mechanical Essentials (9 modules, 10 questions)
    2. Course 2 - Cooling System Principles (6 modules, 10 questions)
    3. Course 3 - Forced Introduction Fundamentals (6 modules, 10 questions)
    4. Course 4 - Engine Management Essentials (10 modules, 10 questions)
    5. Course 5 - Understanding Engine Sensors (9 modules, 10 questions)
    6. Course 6 - Mastering Ignition Systems (8 modules, 10 questions)
    7. Course 7 - Fuel Delivery Essentials (7 modules, 10 questions)
    8. Course 8 - Emissions Control Fundamentals (8 modules, 10 questions)
    9. Course 9 - Understanding Diesel Systems (9 modules, 10 questions)
  10. Course 10 - Common Rail Diesel Explained (6 modules, 10 questions)
   11. Course 11 - Diesel Emissions Technology (7 modules, 10 questions)

Total: 110 questions | Each quiz scored ___ / 10 | Answer keys are separate, in the Answer Key section at the
back, so the quizzes can be printed without the answers.

Course 1: Engine Mechanical Essentials
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                  Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (9): Stroke Engine Principles, Relative Compression Testing, Gasoline Engine Mechanical Checks,
  Best Practice Head and Gasket Testing, Understanding Valve Timing, VVT Cam Phase Type, VVT Cam Changing Type,
  Valve Adjustment Shim Type, Valve Adjustment Rocker Type


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. In a four-stroke engine, which sequence is correct? [STROKE ENGINE PRINCIPLES]
    A. Intake, power, compression, exhaust
    B. Intake, compression, power, exhaust
    C. Compression, intake, exhaust, power
    D. Power, intake, compression, exhaust

2. How many crankshaft degrees does one complete four-stroke cycle take? [STROKE ENGINE PRINCIPLES]
    A. 180 degrees
    B. 360 degrees
    C. 540 degrees
    D. 720 degrees

3. A relative compression test using starter current draw shows one cylinder low. What does that indicate?
[RELATIVE COMPRESSION TESTING]
    A. That cylinder builds less compression, so the starter works less hard on its stroke
    B. The battery is fully charged
    C. That cylinder has higher compression than the others
    D. The starter is overheating

4. Before condemning low compression, which check helps separate ring leakage from valve leakage?
[GASOLINE ENGINE MECHANICAL CHECKS]
    A. A wet compression test - oil added to the cylinder
    B. A fuel pressure test
    C. A cooling system pressure test
    D. A spark output test

5. A chemical block test fluid changes from blue to yellow/combustion colour. What does that suggest?
[BEST PRACTICE HEAD AND GASKET TESTING]
    A. Normal coolant
    B. Combustion gases in the cooling system, such as from a head gasket leak
    C. Low coolant level only
    D. A faulty radiator cap only

Course 1: Engine Mechanical Essentials - Questions 6-10
6. If a timing chain stretches, valve timing will generally: [UNDERSTANDING VALVE TIMING]
    A. Advance
    B. Retard
    C. Stay exactly at specification
    D. Reverse direction

7. A phaser-type VVT system changes valve timing by: [VVT CAM PHASE TYPE]
    A. Swapping to a different cam lobe
    B. Rotating the cam relative to its sprocket
    C. Changing valve lift only
    D. Disconnecting the camshaft

8. A cam-changing (lift/duration switching) system primarily changes: [VVT CAM CHANGING TYPE]
    A. Crankshaft stroke
    B. Which cam lobe profile the valve follows
    C. Compression ratio mechanically
    D. Spark plug gap

9. On a shim-type valvetrain, clearance is too tight. To increase clearance you need a: [VALVE ADJUSTMENT
SHIM TYPE]
    A. Thicker shim
    B. Thinner shim
    C. Longer pushrod
    D. Weaker valve spring

10. On a rocker-type adjustable valvetrain, valve clearance is set with the piston at: [VALVE ADJUSTMENT
ROCKER TYPE]
    A. BDC on the power stroke
    B. TDC on the compression stroke for that cylinder, valves closed
    C. Any position, it does not matter
    D. TDC on the exhaust stroke

Course 2: Cooling System Principles
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                 Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (6): Cooling System Principles, Drive Belt Systems, Cooling System Diagnostics, Cooling Fan Relay
  Control, Thermostat ECM Controlled, Investigating Stray Current Corrosion


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. The thermostat's main job is to: [COOLING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]
    A. Pump coolant
    B. Control minimum operating temperature by blocking flow to the radiator until warm-up
    C. Create coolant pressure
    D. Filter the coolant

2. Raising cooling system pressure with the cap mainly: [COOLING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]
    A. Lowers the boiling point
    B. Raises the boiling point of the coolant
    C. Stops all corrosion
    D. Increases thermostat opening speed only

3. A chirp that changes with accessory load and a glazed, cracked belt most likely needs: [DRIVE BELT
SYSTEMS]
    A. More tension only, never replacement
    B. Belt replacement and pulley alignment check
    C. A shorter belt of any type
    D. Water sprayed on it permanently

4. An engine overheats only at highway speed. A likely cause is: [COOLING SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. A cooling fan fault
    B. A partially restricted radiator or collapsing lower hose
    C. A thermostat stuck open
    D. Cold coolant

5. Pressure-testing the system and the cap checks for: [COOLING SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. Fuel leaks
    B. External/internal leaks and whether the cap holds rated pressure
    C. Spark strength
    D. Oil pressure




Engine Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                           Course 2 - Questions 1-5

Course 2: Cooling System Principles - Questions 6-10
6. The ECM turns the electric fan on mainly based on: [COOLING FAN RELAY CONTROL]
    A. Radio volume
    B. Engine coolant temperature (and A/C request/pressure)
    C. Odometer reading
    D. Fuel level

7. A fan relay coil tests open. The fan will: [COOLING FAN RELAY CONTROL]
    A. Run at high speed
    B. Not run when commanded through that relay
    C. Run continuously
    D. Run only in reverse

8. On an ECM-controlled (map-controlled) thermostat, the ECM can: [THERMOSTAT ECM CONTROLLED]
    A. Move the radiator
    B. Heat the thermostat electrically to open it earlier under load
    C. Disable the water pump permanently
    D. Change coolant colour

9. Stray-current (electrolysis) corrosion in coolant is checked by measuring: [INVESTIGATING STRAY CURRENT
CORROSION]
    A. Voltage between the coolant and battery negative with a voltmeter
    B. Resistance of a spark plug
    C. Fuel pressure
    D. Tyre pressure

10. A common cause of stray current in coolant is: [INVESTIGATING STRAY CURRENT CORROSION]
    A. A missing or corroded engine ground strap
    B. Fresh coolant
    C. A new radiator cap
    D. Correct belt tension

Course 3: Forced Introduction Fundamentals
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                  Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (6): Forced Introduction System Principles, Turbocharger Components Bearings, Twin Scroll
  Turbocharging System Principles, Twin Charge Systems, Understanding Turbo Surge and Flutter, 48 Volt Electric Turbo
  Technology


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. Forced induction increases power mainly by: [FORCED INTRODUCTION SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]
    A. Reducing air density
    B. Increasing the mass of air (and matching fuel) in the cylinder
    C. Raising exhaust backpressure
    D. Slowing the crankshaft

2. A turbocharger shaft is most commonly supported by: [TURBOCHARGER COMPONENTS BEARINGS]
    A. Ball bearings only in all cases
    B. Floating journal (oil-film) bearings fed with pressurised engine oil
    C. Dry plastic bushings
    D. Magnetic levitation with no oil

3. Blue smoke and shaft play after oil starvation most likely mean: [TURBOCHARGER COMPONENTS BEARINGS]
    A. A healthy turbo
    B. Bearing wear - inspect/replace the turbo and fix the oil feed cause
    C. A dirty air filter only
    D. Normal break-in

4. A twin-scroll turbo improves response by: [TWIN SCROLL TURBOCHARGING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]
    A. Mixing all exhaust pulses together
    B. Keeping exhaust pulses from paired cylinders separate to preserve pulse energy
    C. Removing the wastegate
    D. Cooling the intake with fuel

5. A twin-charged engine combines: [TWIN CHARGE SYSTEMS]
    A. Two alternators
    B. A supercharger and a turbocharger
    C. Two radiators
    D. A turbo and a larger exhaust




Engine Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                            Course 3 - Questions 1-5

Course 3: Forced Introduction Fundamentals - Questions
6-10
6. Compressor surge happens when: [UNDERSTANDING TURBO SURGE AND FLUTTER]
    A. Boost is too low at idle
    B. The compressor is asked for pressure the airflow cannot support, so flow stalls/reverses
    C. The wastegate opens normally
    D. Oil pressure rises

7. Flutter/chatter on throttle lift-off can be reduced by a: [UNDERSTANDING TURBO SURGE AND FLUTTER]
    A. Blocked intake
    B. Diverter/blow-off valve that vents or recirculates pressurised air
    C. Tighter wastegate with no control
    D. Removed air filter

8. A 48-volt electric turbo/e-assist mainly helps by: [48 VOLT ELECTRIC TURBO TECHNOLOGY]
    A. Replacing engine oil
    B. Spinning the compressor electrically to cut turbo lag before exhaust energy builds
    C. Powering the headlights only
    D. Charging the 12V battery directly with boost

9. The wastegate controls maximum boost by: [FORCED INTRODUCTION SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]
    A. Closing the throttle
    B. Bypassing exhaust gas around the turbine
    C. Blocking the intercooler
    D. Advancing spark

10. An intercooler's purpose is to: [TURBOCHARGER COMPONENTS BEARINGS]
    A. Heat intake air
    B. Cool the compressed intake air, increasing its density
    C. Filter exhaust gas
    D. Store boost pressure for later

Course 4: Engine Management Essentials
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                    Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (10): Port Fuel Injection Delivery System, Gasoline Injection Fuel Control, Inducing Gasoline Direct
  Injection, Dual Injection Fuel Systems, Understanding Fuel Trims, Understanding Gasoline Scan Tool Data, Throttle
  Actuator Control Systems, Cylinder Deactivation OHV Type, Intake Runner Control System, Intake Runner Control
  Solenoid Type Diagnosis


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. In port fuel injection, fuel is sprayed: [PORT FUEL INJECTION DELIVERY SYSTEM]
    A. Directly into the combustion chamber
    B. Into the intake port, just behind the intake valve
    C. Into the exhaust manifold
    D. Into the throttle bore only on all systems

2. In closed loop, the ECM mainly uses which sensor to trim fuel? [GASOLINE INJECTION FUEL CONTROL]
    A. Oil pressure sensor
    B. Oxygen sensor
    C. Knock sensor only
    D. Vehicle speed sensor

3. Gasoline direct injection differs from PFI because fuel is injected: [INDUCING GASOLINE DIRECT INJECTION]
    A. Before the air filter
    B. Directly into the cylinder at high pressure
    C. Only during the exhaust stroke
    D. Through the spark plug

4. A dual-injection (PFI + GDI) system uses PFI at low load mainly to: [DUAL INJECTION FUEL SYSTEMS]
    A. Increase carbon on intake valves
    B. Reduce particulates and intake-valve deposits and improve low-load running
    C. Disable direct injection permanently
    D. Use more fuel on purpose

5. A large positive long-term fuel trim means the ECM is: [UNDERSTANDING FUEL TRIMS]
    A. Removing fuel
    B. Adding fuel to compensate for a lean condition (e.g. vacuum leak, low pressure)
    C. Seeing a rich condition
    D. In open loop forever

Course 4: Engine Management Essentials - Questions 6-
10
6. Total trim (STFT + LTFT) near +25% at idle but near 0% at cruise suggests: [UNDERSTANDING FUEL TRIMS]
    A. A MAF fault that scales with airflow
    B. An unmetered air/vacuum leak, proportionally biggest at idle
    C. A stuck-open injector
    D. Low tyre pressure

7. Freeze-frame data records: [UNDERSTANDING GASOLINE SCAN TOOL DATA]
    A. Live radio presets
    B. Sensor conditions captured when a DTC set
    C. Only cleared codes
    D. The service history

8. In electronic throttle control, if APP and TPS signals disagree beyond limits, the ECM will typically:
[THROTTLE ACTUATOR CONTROL SYSTEMS]
    A. Ignore it
    B. Enter a reduced-power/limp mode and set a DTC
    C. Open the throttle fully
    D. Disable the brakes

9. OHV cylinder deactivation keeps valves closed on deactivated cylinders by: [CYLINDER DEACTIVATION OHV
TYPE]
    A. Removing the pushrods
    B. Collapsing/special lifters that decouple from the cam lobe
    C. Closing the throttle only
    D. Cutting spark only

10. Intake runner control changes effective runner length to: [INTAKE RUNNER CONTROL SYSTEM]
    A. Only make noise
    B. Use a short path for high rpm and a long path for low-rpm torque
    C. Cool the intake
    D. Meter fuel

Course 5: Understanding Engine Sensors
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                   Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (9): Gasoline Injection Sensors, Narrow Band Oxygen Sensors, Wide Band Oxygen Sensors, Mass
  Airflow Sensors, Hot Film Type Mass Airflow Sensor, Eight Wire Type Mass Airflow Sensor, Wire and Circuits Pull Up and
  Down Circuits, Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor, Throttle Position Sensor


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. The ECM calculates engine load for fueling mainly from: [GASOLINE INJECTION SENSORS]
    A. MAF or MAP plus rpm and temperature inputs
    B. Fuel level only
    C. Ambient light
    D. Brake switch only

2. A healthy narrow-band O2 sensor in closed loop should: [NARROW BAND OXYGEN SENSORS]
    A. Stay fixed at 0.45V
    B. Switch repeatedly above and below about 0.45V, roughly 0.1-0.9V
    C. Stay at 5V
    D. Read battery voltage

3. A wide-band (air-fuel ratio) sensor differs because it can: [WIDE BAND OXYGEN SENSORS]
    A. Only switch rich/lean
    B. Measure the exact air-fuel ratio over a wide range, e.g. 10:1 to 20:1
    C. Replace the MAF
    D. Measure oil pressure

4. A MAF sensor measures: [MASS AIRFLOW SENSORS]
    A. Exhaust volume
    B. The mass of air entering the engine
    C. Fuel mass directly
    D. Intake vacuum only

5. A hot-film MAF stays accurate by keeping its film at a constant temperature. More airflow means: [HOT
FILM TYPE MASS AIRFLOW SENSOR]
    A. Less current needed
    B. More current needed to maintain temperature, which the ECM reads as more airflow
    C. No change in current
    D. The film is switched off

Course 5: Understanding Engine Sensors - Questions 6-
10
6. An 8-wire MAF assembly commonly combines MAF with: [EIGHT WIRE TYPE MASS AIRFLOW SENSOR]
    A. A fuel pump
    B. Intake air temperature and sometimes humidity/barometric sensing in one housing
    C. An oxygen sensor
    D. A knock sensor

7. In a pull-up circuit, the ECM internal resistor pulls the signal voltage up, and the sensor typically: [WIRE
AND CIRCUITS PULL UP AND DOWN CIRCUITS]
    A. Pulls it down toward ground to create the signal
    B. Shorts battery voltage to the ECM
    C. Supplies 12V to the sensor
    D. Disconnects the ground permanently

8. APP sensors use two (or more) tracks mainly to: [ACCELERATOR PEDAL POSITION SENSOR]
    A. Make the pedal heavier
    B. Provide redundancy so the ECM can cross-check for safety
    C. Double the throttle opening
    D. Replace the TPS

9. A TPS signal that drops to 0V briefly while sweeping the throttle indicates: [THROTTLE POSITION SENSOR]
    A. A normal glitch
    B. A worn/open spot in the sensor track - replace the sensor
    C. Low fuel pressure
    D. A good sensor

10. A coolant temperature sensor reading -40 degrees on a warm engine most likely indicates: [GASOLINE
INJECTION SENSORS]
    A. A short to ground
    B. An open circuit (high resistance reads as very cold)
    C. Normal operation
    D. A rich-only fault with no other effect

Course 6: Mastering Ignition Systems
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                       Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (8): Kettering Type Ignition Systems, Spark Plugs, Spark Timing and Dwell Control, Spark Plug and
  Lead Diagnosis, Magneto and CDI, Electronic Switching Ignition Systems, COP and Wasted Spark, Ignition Coil Pack
  Diagnostics


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. In a Kettering (points) system, the condenser/capacitor across the points mainly: [KETTERING TYPE
IGNITION SYSTEMS]
    A. Creates the spark directly
    B. Reduces arcing at the points and speeds primary current collapse
    C. Times the distributor
    D. Charges the battery

2. A plug with a worn, rounded centre electrode and wide gap will: [SPARK PLUGS]
    A. Need less voltage
    B. Require higher firing voltage and may misfire under load
    C. Fire earlier
    D. Run cooler

3. Dwell is best defined as: [SPARK TIMING AND DWELL CONTROL]
    A. Spark duration in the cylinder
    B. The time/angle the primary circuit is on, building coil current before firing
    C. The gap of the plug
    D. Exhaust valve timing

4. A plug lead with carbon tracking on its insulation indicates: [SPARK PLUG AND LEAD DIAGNOSIS]
    A. Normal wear only
    B. Spark leaking to ground along a damaged/contaminated path - replace the lead/plug as needed
    C. High fuel pressure
    D. A good secondary circuit

5. A CDI system differs from inductive ignition because it: [MAGNETO AND CDI]
    A. Stores energy in a capacitor and discharges it rapidly into the coil primary
    B. Uses points only
    C. Has no coil
    D. Fires only at idle




Engine Pop Quizzes - Practice Material                                                              Course 6 - Questions 1-5
COURSE 6 - POP QUIZ, CONTINUED


Course 6: Mastering Ignition Systems - Questions 6-10
6. In electronic (transistor-switched) ignition, the module switches primary current based on: [ELECTRONIC
SWITCHING IGNITION SYSTEMS]
    A. The driver's input only
    B. A crank/cam position pickup signal
    C. Intake vacuum only
    D. Coolant colour

7. In a wasted-spark system, one coil fires two plugs at once. The 'waste' spark occurs on the: [COP AND
WASTED SPARK]
    A. Compression stroke
    B. Exhaust stroke of the companion cylinder
    C. Intake stroke
    D. Power stroke

8. Coil-on-plug (COP) gives an advantage because each coil has: [COP AND WASTED SPARK]
    A. Less dwell time available
    B. More time to saturate between firings and no plug leads to lose energy
    C. Only one cylinder to fire at any speed with no control
    D. No primary circuit

9. A coil pack secondary that reads open/infinite resistance most likely means: [IGNITION COIL PACK
DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. A good coil
    B. An open secondary winding - the coil will not fire that output
    C. Low primary resistance only
    D. A fouled plug only

10. Advancing spark timing too far under load is most likely to cause: [SPARK TIMING AND DWELL CONTROL]
    A. Retarded combustion
    B. Detonation/knock and possible engine damage
    C. A weaker alternator
    D. Low oil pressure

Course 7: Fuel Delivery Essentials
Name:                                    Date:
                                                                                 Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (7): Fuel Delivery System Mechanical Checks, Fuel Delivery System Electrical Checks, Injector
  Diagnostics, Fuel Pump Control Module Checks, Fuel Pressure Regulator Performance, Introducing Ethanol Fuel, E85
  Fuel Flex Vehicles


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. Low fuel pressure with good pump voltage - the next mechanical check is: [FUEL DELIVERY SYSTEM
MECHANICAL CHECKS]
    A. Replace the ECM
    B. Check for a restricted filter, kinked line or weak pump, and check volume/flow as well as pressure
    C. Advance the timing
    D. Replace the spark plugs

2. Voltage-drop testing the pump ground while the pump runs shows 1.2V. That means: [FUEL DELIVERY
SYSTEM ELECTRICAL CHECKS]
    A. A perfect ground
    B. Excessive resistance in the ground - the pump is losing 1.2V it needs
    C. The pump is new
    D. Normal on all vehicles, ignore it

3. An injector that clicks but delivers no fuel could have: [INJECTOR DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. A clogged inlet screen/nozzle or no fuel pressure to it
    B. Perfect delivery
    C. Too much fuel pressure only
    D. A good spray pattern by definition

4. Comparing injector current ramps, one injector shows a much lower, slower rise. That suggests:
[INJECTOR DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. A shorted coil
    B. Higher circuit resistance or a partially open injector coil
    C. A good injector
    D. Low battery state of charge only

5. A fuel pump control module varies pump speed mainly by: [FUEL PUMP CONTROL MODULE CHECKS]
    A. Changing fuel octane
    B. Pulse-width modulating voltage to the pump to match demand
    C. Blocking the return line permanently
    D. Switching the injectors off

Course 7: Fuel Delivery Essentials - Questions 6-10
6. On a vacuum-referenced regulator, fuel pressure at idle (high vacuum) should be: [FUEL PRESSURE
REGULATOR PERFORMANCE]
    A. Higher than at wide-open throttle
    B. Lower than with the vacuum hose disconnected
    C. Exactly battery voltage
    D. Zero

7. Fuel found inside the regulator's vacuum hose means: [FUEL PRESSURE REGULATOR PERFORMANCE]
    A. Normal operation
    B. A ruptured regulator diaphragm - replace the regulator
    C. A clogged air filter
    D. Good fuel pressure

8. Compared with pure gasoline, ethanol contains: [INTRODUCING ETHANOL FUEL]
    A. More energy per gallon
    B. Less energy per gallon, so more volume is needed for the same work
    C. No oxygen
    D. Twice the energy

9. A flex-fuel vehicle knows the ethanol percentage mainly by: [E85 FUEL FLEX VEHICLES]
    A. The fuel cap colour
    B. A fuel composition (ethanol content) sensor or calculated/virtual sensing from O2 feedback
    C. The odometer
    D. Intake air temperature alone

10. Running E85 in a non-flex-fuel vehicle is risky mainly because: [E85 FUEL FLEX VEHICLES]
    A. It has too much energy
    B. The system may not add enough fuel (lean running) and materials may not be ethanol-compatible
    C. It instantly raises compression
    D. It disables the fuel pump relay

  Modules covered (8): Vehicle Emissions Principles, Exhaust Gas Recirculation, Vented Evaporative System, Gasoline
  Exhaust Emission Diagnostics, Two-Way Catalytic Converters, Three-Way Catalytic Converters, Catalytic Converter

Circle the best answer for each question.

1. NOx forms mainly when: [VEHICLE EMISSIONS PRINCIPLES]
    A. Combustion is very cold
    B. Combustion temperatures are very high
    C. The engine is off
    D. Fuel is unburned only

2. Unburned hydrocarbons (HC) rise most directly with: [VEHICLE EMISSIONS PRINCIPLES]
    A. A perfect burn
    B. Misfire or incomplete combustion
    C. Normal closed-loop control
    D. A hot catalytic converter

3. EGR reduces NOx by: [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]
    A. Adding oxygen
    B. Recirculating inert exhaust to lower peak combustion temperature
    C. Enriching the mixture heavily
    D. Raising combustion temperature

4. EGR stuck open at idle will typically cause: [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]
    A. Smooth idle
    B. Rough idle, stalling or hesitation
    C. Higher NOx only
    D. No drivability effect

5. The EVAP system's job is to: [VENTED EVAPORATIVE SYSTEM]
    A. Vent fuel vapours freely to air
    B. Capture fuel vapours in a charcoal canister and purge them into the engine to burn
    C. Cool the fuel tank
    D. Meter liquid fuel to the injectors

10
6. High CO on a gas analyser most directly indicates: [GASOLINE EXHAUST EMISSION DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. A lean mixture
    B. A rich mixture / incomplete combustion with excess fuel
    C. A vacuum leak only
    D. Low HC

7. A two-way (oxidation) converter converts: [TWO-WAY CATALYTIC CONVERTERS]
    A. NOx to nitrogen
    B. HC and CO into water and CO2
    C. CO2 into oxygen
    D. Fuel into HC

8. A three-way converter can reduce NOx and oxidise HC/CO at the same time only when: [THREE-WAY
CATALYTIC CONVERTERS]
    A. The mixture is always rich
    B. The air-fuel ratio cycles tightly around stoichiometry (14.7:1)
    C. The engine is cold
    D. Oxygen sensors are disconnected

9. A converter stores and releases which gas to work over the rich/lean swing? [CATALYTIC CONVERTER
EFFICIENCY]
    A. Nitrogen
    B. Oxygen (in its cerium washcoat)
    C. Carbon monoxide
    D. Fuel vapour

10. The ECM judges converter efficiency mainly by comparing: [CATALYTIC EFFICIENCY DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. Front and rear MAF signals
    B. Upstream and downstream O2 sensor switching activity
    C. Fuel pressure to oil pressure
    D. Intake and exhaust temperature only

Course 9: Understanding Diesel Systems
Name:                                    Date:

  Modules covered (9): Diesel Unit Injection, Hydraulic Electronic Unit Injection, Diesel Fuel Delivery Low Pressure
  Supply, Diesel Fuel Delivery High Pressure Supply, Two Stroke Diesel Technology, Diesel Engine Mechanical Checks,
  Glow Plug Operation, Indirect Glow Plug System Testing Procedures, Direct Glow Plug System Testing Procedures


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. In a unit injector system, each injector: [DIESEL UNIT INJECTION]
    A. Only meters fuel, pressure comes from the rail
    B. Combines pump and injector in one unit, usually cam-driven, per cylinder
    C. Is powered by spark
    D. Feeds all cylinders from one body

2. HEUI injectors are actuated for injection pressure by: [HYDRAULIC ELECTRONIC UNIT INJECTION]
    A. High-pressure engine oil acting on an intensifier piston
    B. A spark plug
    C. Vacuum
    D. The alternator

3. Air entering the low-pressure diesel supply most commonly causes: [DIESEL FUEL DELIVERY LOW
PRESSURE SUPPLY]
    A. Smooth running
    B. Hard starting, stalling or no-start - diesels need a solid, air-free fuel supply
    C. Higher power
    D. Lower emissions only

4. On a high-pressure diesel pump system, a failed pressure control will most likely show as: [DIESEL FUEL
DELIVERY HIGH PRESSURE SUPPLY]
    A. Normal pressure always
    B. Rail/injection pressure too low (hard start, low power) or too high (rough, noisy running)
    C. A tyre fault
    D. A coolant leak

5. A two-stroke diesel gets its intake air mainly by: [TWO STROKE DIESEL TECHNOLOGY]
    A. Natural vacuum only
    B. A blower/supercharger (and often a turbo) forcing air through ports, with exhaust valves in the head
    C. A carburettor
    D. Glow plugs

    A. Sparking the fuel
    B. Heating the air in/near the chamber so injected fuel ignites reliably
    C. Pumping fuel
    D. Turning the starter

[INDIRECT GLOW PLUG SYSTEM TESTING PROCEDURES]
    A. No effect on any engine
    B. Rough, smoky cold starting on that cylinder until it warms up
    C. Instant overheating
    D. A charging fault

9. For a direct-injection glow plug system, a current-draw (amp clamp) test is useful because it: [DIRECT
GLOW PLUG SYSTEM TESTING PROCEDURES]
    A. Measures fuel pressure
    B. Shows each plug is actually drawing current/heating without removing the plugs
    C. Tests the starter only
    D. Replaces all other tests in every case

10. White smoke and extended cranking on a cold morning, clearing as the engine warms, points first to:
[GLOW PLUG OPERATION]
    A. A good glow system
    B. Glow plug or glow control faults (or low compression) on one or more cylinders
    C. A hot thermostat
    D. Excess fuel octane

Circle the best answer for each question.

1. 'Common rail' means: [INTRODUCING COMMON RAIL DIESEL]
    A. All injectors share one high-pressure accumulator (the rail) separate from injection timing
    B. Injectors are driven by the cam only
    C. Fuel is delivered by gravity
    D. There is one injector for all cylinders

2. Typical common-rail pressures are in the range of: [CRD FUEL DELIVERY]
    A. 30-60 psi
    B. About 5,000-30,000 psi (roughly 350-2,000+ bar) depending on system and load
    C. 500 psi maximum on all systems
    D. Vacuum

3. If rail pressure cannot build while cranking, a common cause is: [CRD FUEL DELIVERY]
    A. A good high-pressure pump by definition
    B. Excessive injector leak-back, a weak pump or a suction/supply fault starving the pump
    C. High tyre pressure
    D. A clean fuel filter guaranteed

4. A key advantage of electronic CRD control is multiple injection events per cycle, used to: [CRD
ELECTRONIC CONTROLS]
    A. Waste fuel
    B. Use pilot injection to soften combustion noise, main injection for power, and post injection for aftertreatment
    C. Disable the turbo
    D. Replace glow plugs on all engines

5. The rail pressure sensor and pressure regulator work together so the ECM can: [CRD ELECTRONIC
CONTROLS]
    A. Ignore rail pressure
    B. Hold actual rail pressure at the target for load and speed
    C. Set tyre pressure
    D. Control the cooling fan only

6. When a CRD injector is replaced, its code must be entered into the ECM because: [CRD INJECTOR CODING]

    B. Each injector's flow correction/classification differs slightly, and the ECM trims delivery using that code
    C. Coding changes the rail pressure mechanically
    D. Coding is never needed on CRD

7. Skipping injector coding after replacement can cause: [CRD INJECTOR CODING]
    A. Nothing at all
    B. Rough idle, uneven cylinder balance, smoke or DTCs from incorrect per-cylinder fueling
    C. A flat tyre
    D. Low coolant

8. Swirl/throttle flaps in a CRD intake mainly help to: [CRD INTAKE AND EXHAUST SYSTEM]
    A. Block air permanently
    B. Control air motion and EGR mixing at low load for cleaner, more stable combustion
    C. Increase rail pressure
    D. Cool the fuel rail

indicates: [CRD INJECTOR LEAK BACK TESTING]

    B. Internal wear/leakage in that injector - it is stealing rail pressure
    C. A good seal
    D. A blocked return line to all injectors

    B. At cranking or idle into graduated containers over a set time, comparing cylinders
    C. By listening to the exhaust

Course 11: Diesel Emissions Technology
Name:                                     Date:
                                                                                 Score: ___ / 10



  Modules covered (7): Vehicle Emission Principles, Exhaust Gas Recirculation, NOx Type Catalytic Converters, DPF
  Diesel Particular Filter, DPF Flow Diagnostics, Selective Catalytic Reduction, DPF Regeneration


Circle the best answer for each question.

1. Diesel exhaust aftertreatment has to deal mainly with which two pollutants that trade off against each
other? [VEHICLE EMISSION PRINCIPLES]
    A. CO and HC only
    B. NOx and particulate matter (soot)
    C. Oxygen and nitrogen
    D. Water and CO2

2. On a diesel, high-rate or cooled EGR lowers NOx but can increase: [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]
    A. Soot/particulate loading and DPF burden
    B. Tyre wear
    C. Rail pressure automatically
    D. Glow plug life

3. A lean NOx trap (NOx storage catalyst) works by: [NOX TYPE CATALYTIC CONVERTERS]
    A. Burning soot only
    B. Storing NOx during lean running, then releasing and reducing it during a brief rich purge
    C. Adding DEF
    D. Filtering particulates

4. A DPF (diesel particulate filter) does what? [DPF DIESEL PARTICULAR FILTER]
    A. Converts NOx to nitrogen
    B. Traps soot in a wall-flow filter until it is burned off in regeneration
    C. Stores fuel vapour
    D. Cools exhaust gas only

5. DPF soot loading is estimated mainly from: [DPF FLOW DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. Exhaust colour alone
    B. Differential pressure across the DPF (plus a model) - higher pressure drop means more loading/restriction
    C. Fuel level
    D. Intake air temperature only

Course 11: Diesel Emissions Technology - Questions 6-10
6. A differential pressure sensor hose that is split or blocked will cause: [DPF FLOW DIAGNOSTICS]
    A. Accurate readings
    B. False loading readings, failed or unnecessary regenerations, and related DTCs
    C. Better fuel economy guaranteed
    D. No symptoms ever

7. SCR reduces NOx using: [SELECTIVE CATALYTIC REDUCTION]
    A. Gasoline
    B. DEF (urea/AdBlue), which forms ammonia that converts NOx to nitrogen and water over the SCR catalyst
    C. Engine oil
    D. Coolant

8. If DEF runs empty or quality is poor, the system will typically: [SELECTIVE CATALYTIC REDUCTION]
    A. Run normally with no warning
    B. Warn the driver, then limit torque/speed or prevent restart until corrected
    C. Increase power
    D. Disable the DPF only

9. Active DPF regeneration cleans the filter by: [DPF REGENERATION]
    A. Washing it with water while driving
    B. Raising exhaust temperature (often with post-injected fuel) to burn soot to ash/CO2
    C. Removing and shaking it at every stop
    D. Cooling the exhaust

10. Repeatedly interrupting regeneration with short trips most likely leads to: [DPF REGENERATION]
    A. A cleaner filter
    B. Rising soot load, more frequent regens, oil dilution from post-injection, and eventually a forced/service regen
    or warning light
    C. Instant engine failure in all cases
    D. Lower soot forever

Quiz 1: Engine Mechanical Essentials - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                  Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - One cycle needs intake, compression, power and exhaust - two crank revolutions, 720 degrees. [STROKE
ENGINE PRINCIPLES]


2. D - Each stroke is 180 degrees; four strokes total 720 degrees. [STROKE ENGINE PRINCIPLES]

3. A - Less compression means less load, so current dips on that cylinder's compression stroke. [RELATIVE
COMPRESSION TESTING]


4. A - If wet compression rises sharply, oil helped the rings seal, pointing to ring/bore wear. [GASOLINE ENGINE
MECHANICAL CHECKS]


5. B - The fluid reacts to CO2 from combustion gases entering the coolant. [BEST PRACTICE HEAD AND GASKET
TESTING]


6. B - Stretch delays cam rotation relative to the crank, retarding valve events. [UNDERSTANDING VALVE TIMING]

7. B - A cam phaser advances or retards the whole cam by rotating it relative to drive. [VVT CAM PHASE TYPE]

8. B - It switches between lobe profiles to change lift and duration, not just phase. [VVT CAM CHANGING TYPE]

9. B - A thinner shim leaves more gap between cam lobe and follower. [VALVE ADJUSTMENT SHIM TYPE]

10. B - Both valves must be fully closed on the base circle - TDC compression. [VALVE ADJUSTMENT ROCKER TYPE]

Quiz 2: Cooling System Principles - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                 Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - It stays closed during warm-up, then opens to regulate temperature. [COOLING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]

2. B - About 3 degrees F boiling-point rise per psi of pressure. [COOLING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]

3. B - Glazing and cracks mean the belt is worn; misalignment causes chirp and repeat wear. [DRIVE BELT SYSTEMS]

4. B - Fans matter most at low speed; high-speed overheating points to flow restriction. [COOLING SYSTEM
DIAGNOSTICS]


5. B - A system that will not hold pressure leaks; a cap that vents early lowers boiling point. [COOLING SYSTEM
DIAGNOSTICS]


6. B - ECT is the primary input, with A/C request as another common trigger. [COOLING FAN RELAY CONTROL]

7. B - An open coil cannot create the magnetic field that closes the relay contacts. [COOLING FAN RELAY CONTROL]

8. B - A heater element lets the ECM open the thermostat sooner than wax alone would. [THERMOSTAT ECM
CONTROLLED]


9. A - Voltage in the coolant above a small threshold indicates electrical current damaging metals. [INVESTIGATING
STRAY CURRENT CORROSION]


10. A - Poor grounds force current to find a path through the coolant and heater core/radiator. [INVESTIGATING
STRAY CURRENT CORROSION]

Quiz 3: Forced Introduction Fundamentals - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                  Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - More air mass allows more fuel to burn per cycle. [FORCED INTRODUCTION SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]

2. B - Most turbos float the shaft on pressurised oil films; oil supply and drain are critical. [TURBOCHARGER
COMPONENTS BEARINGS]


3. B - Oil starvation destroys turbo bearings quickly; the root cause must be fixed. [TURBOCHARGER COMPONENTS
BEARINGS]


4. B - Separate scrolls keep pulse energy and reduce interference, spooling the turbo sooner. [TWIN SCROLL
TURBOCHARGING SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]


5. B - The supercharger gives low-speed boost; the turbo takes over at higher speed/flow. [TWIN CHARGE SYSTEMS]

6. B - Surge is an unstable stall - often heard as chattering when the throttle closes under boost. [UNDERSTANDING
TURBO SURGE AND FLUTTER]


7. B - Venting the pressure spike keeps the compressor out of surge. [UNDERSTANDING TURBO SURGE AND
FLUTTER]


8. B - Electric drive spools the compressor at low rpm where exhaust energy is weak. [48 VOLT ELECTRIC TURBO
TECHNOLOGY]


9. B - Bypassing exhaust limits turbine speed and therefore boost. [FORCED INTRODUCTION SYSTEM PRINCIPLES]

10. B - Compression heats air; cooling it restores density and reduces knock tendency. [TURBOCHARGER
COMPONENTS BEARINGS]

Quiz 4: Engine Management Essentials - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                   Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - PFI injectors sit in the intake port/runner aimed at the back of the intake valve. [PORT FUEL INJECTION
DELIVERY SYSTEM]


2. B - O2 feedback drives short-term correction around stoichiometry in closed loop. [GASOLINE INJECTION FUEL
CONTROL]


3. B - GDI uses a high-pressure pump and injectors in the chamber, often 500-3,000+ psi. [INDUCING GASOLINE
DIRECT INJECTION]


4. B - Port fuel washes the intake valves and helps low-load emissions; GDI dominates at higher load. [DUAL
INJECTION FUEL SYSTEMS]


5. B - Positive trim = adding fuel because the system was running lean. [UNDERSTANDING FUEL TRIMS]

6. B - A fixed vacuum leak is a large share of idle airflow but a small share at cruise. [UNDERSTANDING FUEL TRIMS]

7. B - Freeze frame snapshots key PIDs at the moment the fault matured. [UNDERSTANDING GASOLINE SCAN TOOL
DATA]


8. B - Redundant, opposing sensors are cross-checked; disagreement triggers a safe default. [THROTTLE ACTUATOR
CONTROL SYSTEMS]


9. B - Switching lifters collapse so pushrods do not lift the valves, while fuel and spark are also cut. [CYLINDER
DEACTIVATION OHV TYPE]


10. B - Long runners favour low-speed torque; short runners favour high-speed breathing. [INTAKE RUNNER
CONTROL SYSTEM]

Quiz 5: Understanding Engine Sensors - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                  Second score: ___ / 10


1. A - Airflow/air pressure, rpm and temperatures define how much fuel a cylinder fill needs. [GASOLINE INJECTION
SENSORS]


2. B - Switching shows it sensing rich/lean crossings around stoichiometry. [NARROW BAND OXYGEN SENSORS]

3. B - Its pump-cell current is proportional to lambda across a broad range. [WIDE BAND OXYGEN SENSORS]

4. B - Fuel is matched to air mass, so MAF is a primary fueling input. [MASS AIRFLOW SENSORS]

5. B - Moving air cools the film; the heating current needed is the airflow signal. [HOT FILM TYPE MASS AIRFLOW
SENSOR]


6. B - Extra wires serve the additional sensing elements built into the housing. [EIGHT WIRE TYPE MASS AIRFLOW
SENSOR]


7. A - Many thermistor/switch circuits work this way: the sensor pulls the 5V reference down. [WIRE AND CIRCUITS
PULL UP AND DOWN CIRCUITS]


8. B - If the two APP signals do not agree in their set ratio, a fault is set. [ACCELERATOR PEDAL POSITION SENSOR]

9. B - Dropouts during a smooth sweep show a dead spot in the resistive track. [THROTTLE POSITION SENSOR]

10. B - On an NTC thermistor circuit, open/high resistance = the coldest reading; it also causes over-fueling.
[GASOLINE INJECTION SENSORS]

Quiz 6: Mastering Ignition Systems - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                 Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - It absorbs the primary surge as points open, sharpening the magnetic collapse. [KETTERING TYPE IGNITION
SYSTEMS]


2. B - A larger, worn gap takes more voltage to jump, especially under cylinder pressure. [SPARK PLUGS]

3. B - Enough dwell saturates the coil; too little weakens the spark, too much overheats it. [SPARK TIMING AND
DWELL CONTROL]


4. B - Tracking is a leakage path that steals spark energy, usually under load. [SPARK PLUG AND LEAD DIAGNOSIS]

5. A - Capacitor discharge gives a very fast, high-voltage rise, common on small engines. [MAGNETO AND CDI]

6. B - The pickup tells the module when to turn primary current off and fire the coil. [ELECTRONIC SWITCHING
IGNITION SYSTEMS]


7. B - Companion cylinders are at TDC together; one is on compression, the other wastes its spark on exhaust. [COP
AND WASTED SPARK]


8. B - One coil per cylinder means long dwell availability and no secondary leads. [COP AND WASTED SPARK]

9. B - No continuity in the secondary means no complete high-voltage path. [IGNITION COIL PACK DIAGNOSTICS]

10. B - Too-early ignition raises peak pressure and temperature, promoting knock. [SPARK TIMING AND DWELL
CONTROL]

Quiz 7: Fuel Delivery Essentials - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                   Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - Pressure alone can mislead; a restriction or worn pump fails on volume under demand. [FUEL DELIVERY
SYSTEM MECHANICAL CHECKS]


2. B - More than about 0.2-0.5V drop on a ground under load is excessive. [FUEL DELIVERY SYSTEM ELECTRICAL
CHECKS]


3. A - Electrical operation does not prove hydraulic delivery; check pressure and spray/flow. [INJECTOR
DIAGNOSTICS]


4. B - Current ramp shape reveals coil resistance and pintle movement faults. [INJECTOR DIAGNOSTICS]

5. B - PWM control delivers only the needed flow, cutting noise, heat and current draw. [FUEL PUMP CONTROL
MODULE CHECKS]


6. B - Vacuum helps pull fuel through the injector, so rail pressure drops to keep the differential constant. [FUEL
PRESSURE REGULATOR PERFORMANCE]


7. B - Fuel should never cross into the vacuum side; it also causes rich running. [FUEL PRESSURE REGULATOR
PERFORMANCE]


8. B - Ethanol is oxygenated but energy-poor per gallon versus gasoline. [INTRODUCING ETHANOL FUEL]

9. B - Content sensing lets the ECM adjust fuel volume, spark and cold-start strategy. [E85 FUEL FLEX VEHICLES]

10. B - Non-flex systems lack the trim range, sensing and compatible seals/hoses for high ethanol. [E85 FUEL FLEX
VEHICLES]

Quiz 8: Emissions Control Fundamentals - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - High temperature and pressure combine nitrogen and oxygen into NOx. [VEHICLE EMISSIONS PRINCIPLES]

2. B - Fuel that does not burn leaves as HC - misfire is the classic cause. [VEHICLE EMISSIONS PRINCIPLES]

3. B - Diluted, cooler combustion produces far less NOx. [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]

4. B - Idle needs no dilution; excess EGR destabilises combustion. [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]

5. B - Vapours are stored, then purged under ECM control instead of escaping. [VENTED EVAPORATIVE SYSTEM]

6. B - CO is partially burned fuel - a rich-running signature. [GASOLINE EXHAUST EMISSION DIAGNOSTICS]

7. B - Two-way cats oxidise HC and CO; they do not reduce NOx. [TWO-WAY CATALYTIC CONVERTERS]

8. B - The 14.7:1 window is where both reduction and oxidation work together. [THREE-WAY CATALYTIC
CONVERTERS]


9. B - Oxygen storage smooths the swings and is the basis of efficiency monitoring. [CATALYTIC CONVERTER
EFFICIENCY]


10. B - A good cat makes the rear O2 switch much slower/flatter than the front. [CATALYTIC EFFICIENCY
DIAGNOSTICS]

Quiz 9: Understanding Diesel Systems - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                   Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - The pumping element and nozzle are one unit per cylinder - no common rail. [DIESEL UNIT INJECTION]

2. A - HEUI uses high-pressure oil to intensify fuel pressure inside the injector. [HYDRAULIC ELECTRONIC UNIT
INJECTION]


3. B - Diesel injection cannot compress air in the lines; leaks on the suction side are critical. [DIESEL FUEL DELIVERY
LOW PRESSURE SUPPLY]


4. B - Injection pressure defines atomisation and quantity; control faults hit starting and power first. [DIESEL FUEL
DELIVERY HIGH PRESSURE SUPPLY]


5. B - Two-stroke diesels cannot breathe on piston vacuum alone, so they are scavenged by a blower. [TWO STROKE
DIESEL TECHNOLOGY]


6. B - Compression ignition typically needs roughly 16:1-22:1 and healthy cranking compression. [DIESEL ENGINE
MECHANICAL CHECKS]


7. B - They pre-heat and often post-heat for smoother, cleaner cold running. [GLOW PLUG OPERATION]

8. B - That cylinder lacks pre-heat, so it misfires cold and makes white smoke. [INDIRECT GLOW PLUG SYSTEM
TESTING PROCEDURES]


9. B - Comparing per-plug current finds open or weak plugs quickly. [DIRECT GLOW PLUG SYSTEM TESTING
PROCEDURES]


10. B - Unburned fuel vapour from cold cylinders is white; it clears with heat. [GLOW PLUG OPERATION]

Engine Pop Quizzes - Answer Key                                                                         Quiz 9 - Answer Key

Quiz 10: Common Rail Diesel Explained - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                    Second score: ___ / 10


1. A - Pressure generation and injection are separated - the rail stores pressurised fuel for all injectors.
[INTRODUCING COMMON RAIL DIESEL]


2. B - Modern CRD runs into the thousands of bar for fine atomisation and multiple injections. [CRD FUEL DELIVERY]

3. B - The pump cannot build pressure if fuel leaks back or never reaches it. [CRD FUEL DELIVERY]

4. B - Pilot/post events cut diesel knock and support DPF regeneration. [CRD ELECTRONIC CONTROLS]

5. B - It is a closed loop: sensor feedback, regulator/pump control correction. [CRD ELECTRONIC CONTROLS]

6. B - The IMA/C2I-type code tells the ECM that injector's measured flow deviation. [CRD INJECTOR CODING]

7. B - Without its correction, that cylinder is over- or under-fueled relative to the others. [CRD INJECTOR CODING]

8. B - Air-motion control improves mixing, especially with EGR at part load. [CRD INTAKE AND EXHAUST SYSTEM]

9. B - Excess return flow is a worn injector bypassing fuel instead of injecting it. [CRD INJECTOR LEAK BACK TESTING]

10. B - Equal-time graduated bottles make the faulty injector obvious by volume. [CRD INJECTOR LEAK BACK
TESTING]

Engine Pop Quizzes - Answer Key                                                                         Quiz 10 - Answer Key
ANSWER KEY - QUIZ 11 OF 11


Quiz 11: Diesel Emissions Technology - Answer Key
Retake date:                                                  Second score: ___ / 10


1. B - Cutting NOx in-cylinder tends to raise soot, and vice versa - hence DPF plus NOx aftertreatment. [VEHICLE
EMISSION PRINCIPLES]


2. A - Cooler, diluted combustion makes less NOx but more particulates to trap. [EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION]

3. B - It stores NOx as nitrates, then a rich excursion converts it to nitrogen. [NOX TYPE CATALYTIC CONVERTERS]

4. B - Soot accumulates in the filter and must be oxidised periodically. [DPF DIESEL PARTICULAR FILTER]

5. B - Pressure before vs. after the filter rises as soot and ash restrict flow. [DPF FLOW DIAGNOSTICS]

6. B - The ECM trusts that pressure signal - a hose fault corrupts every DPF decision. [DPF FLOW DIAGNOSTICS]

7. B - Dosed urea is the reductant that makes lean NOx conversion possible. [SELECTIVE CATALYTIC REDUCTION]

8. B - Emissions rules require inducement - warnings escalating to derate/no-restart. [SELECTIVE CATALYTIC
REDUCTION]


9. B - Temperatures around 600C oxidise the trapped soot. [DPF REGENERATION]

10. B - The filter never finishes cleaning, so load climbs and fuel ends up in the oil. [DPF REGENERATION]

  9/10 or better before moving on.
